hero.line2: Everything that actually moves the needle.
hero.intro: You do not need to pay for the knowledge to start an online career. Almost everything worth learning is already no-cost: from the world's best universities, from the companies whose tools you will use, from your own government, and from a few genuinely great teachers on YouTube. The hard part was never access. It is knowing which no-cost thing is worth your week, and how to turn it into proof instead of a pile of half-finished tabs. That is what this page is for.
hero.creed: It is only worth the tab if it does not cost you a month you cannot get back. The skill is not finding a course. It is judging one before it takes your time, and finishing it with something to show.

judge.title: How to judge any open course before it takes your week.
judge.lead: There is an ocean of open learning, and most of it is a comfortable way to feel productive without becoming more hireable. Run any course, including the ones we list below, through these five questions first. The ones worth your time survive all five.

tests.q: Does it end in a real artifact?
tests.why: A course you finish with nothing to show taught you nothing a client can see. Prefer the ones that make you build something, a project, a page, a working sheet, over the ones that just fill your head and hand you a certificate.

tests.q: Is it from the source, or a reseller?
tests.why: The vendor's or institution's own site, like the real university or the real tool maker, is current, no-cost, and correct. A stranger repackaging it on a course marketplace is usually neither no-cost nor up to date. Go to the source.

AI and tools change every few months. A 2020 course on an AI product is a museum piece. Check when it was last updated before you trust a single click of it, especially for anything with AI in the title.

tests.q: Open to audit, or gated by a paywall?
tests.why: Plenty of open courses gate the certificate, the exam, or the real lessons behind a trial that wants a card. Read the fine print for ninety seconds before you commit an afternoon, so the open part is actually the part you need.

tests.q: Does it teach the method or the buttons?
tests.why: A tutorial on where today's buttons are expires with the next redesign. The transferable method, why the tool exists and what it is really for, does not. Learn the version that survives the update.

judge.note: If a course fails these, it is not bad. It is just not worth your scarce hours right now. Close the tab without guilt.

shelf.kicker: The shelf · go to the source
shelf.title: The resources we actually point people to.
shelf.lead: Curated, not endless: a shelf, not a warehouse. Each one is no-cost or open-to-audit, from the source, and chosen because it ends in something you can use. Open the ones that fit your lane, ignore the rest. We link the primary site every time, so you always land on the real, current version.

groups.title: AI fluency, start here
groups.note: The single highest-leverage no-cost study you can do this month. Learn to work with AI as a professional, not a tourist. Do the first one before anything else on this shelf.

items.title: AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations
items.why: A no-cost, few-hour course on the four habits of working with AI well: Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence. The single highest-leverage no-cost thing on this shelf. Do it first.

items.title: Google AI Essentials
items.why: A hands-on intro to using generative AI at work in under five hours, no coding needed. On Coursera with a trial and financial aid. The fundamentals are worth the time.

groups.title: Philippine government & public, open by right
groups.note: Your taxes already paid for these. No-cost digital-skills training and certificates from Philippine public programs. It is yours by right, so take the certificate, then go build the proof that actually gets you hired.

items.title: TESDA Online Program
items.why: The government's open course platform: dozens of programs with National Certificates, from web and mobile development to bookkeeping. Your taxes paid for it, and the NC is a real, recognised credential.

items.title: DICT digital skills (SPARK)
items.why: No-cost government training built for online freelancing: social media, graphic design, web dev, AI and data science, with a freelancing on-ramp. Formerly DigitalJobsPH, now delivered as SPARK.

groups.title: Craft skills, from the people who made the tools
groups.note: The companies whose software you will use, and the universities, give their courses away on purpose: a skilled user is a lifelong one. Pick the ones in your niche and finish with a project, not just a badge.

items.title: freeCodeCamp
items.why: A charity's complete, no-cost curriculum in web development, data, and Python: thousands of hours, real certifications, and projects you build to earn them.

items.title: CS50: Intro to Computer Science
items.why: Harvard's famous intro to computer science, open to audit. The best single foundation if you want to truly understand how software works. Optional paid certificate.

items.title: HubSpot Academy
items.why: No-cost, well-respected certifications in marketing, sales, CRM, and customer service, directly useful for ops, social media, and support roles.

items.title: Google Skillshop
items.why: Google's no-cost certifications in Google Ads and Analytics, the credentials clients actually recognise for marketing and data work.

items.title: Meta Blueprint
items.why: Meta's 100+ open courses and no-cost certification exams for Facebook and Instagram advertising, the standard training for social-media and paid-ads gigs.

items.title: Canva Design School
items.why: No-cost design courses and certifications from Canva: color, type, and layout basics, taught inside the exact tool most social and design gigs use daily.

items.title: The All-Remote Handbook
items.why: The best no-cost resource anywhere on how async remote work really works, from a company that has done it at scale for a decade. Read it and out-communicate people with five years on you.

groups.title: YouTube, teachers worth your time
groups.note: The best of YouTube rivals any paid course. These channels are durable and genuinely teach a craft. Watch to build, not to binge.

items.title: freeCodeCamp.org
items.why: 700+ full-length open courses on coding, data, and AI: some of the best long-form technical teaching anywhere, and new ones weekly.

items.title: Kevin Stratvert
items.why: Fast, clear tutorials on AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot), Excel, and everyday software, perfect for learning a tool the week a client needs it.

items.title: Grow with Google
items.why: Google's own channel for career and digital-skills training, job-ready skills straight from the source.

items.title: Google Career Certificates
items.why: Guidance and real graduate stories for career-changers moving into UX, data, IT, and support roles.

groups.title: Be a real business, taxes & benefits
groups.note: The unglamorous half that separates a hobby from a career: how to register, file your taxes, and get your own benefits as a self-employed Filipino. Being BIR-registered and invoice-ready is itself a rate differentiator, because serious clients can book you as a real supplier.

items.title: Bureau of Internal Revenue
items.why: Register as self-employed with BIR Form 1901 and choose the 8% flat tax on gross income over ₱250,000. The annual registration fee was scrapped in 2024. This is the official source, straight from the agency.

items.title: Freelancer tax guide + online filing
items.why: A plain-English walk-through of BIR registration, the 8% rate, and the filing deadlines, plus a tool that files for you. Published 2025; check for a newer edition before trusting a specific deadline. Start here if the BIR site feels like a maze.

items.title: SSS for the self-employed
items.why: Register as a self-employed member for sickness, maternity, disability, and retirement benefits. No employer means you fund this yourself, so start early and stay consistent.

items.title: PhilHealth
items.why: Register as a self-earning individual for health coverage. It is required for the self-employed, and it is cheap protection against a hospital bill wiping out your savings.

items.title: Pag-IBIG Fund
items.why: Technically voluntary for freelancers, but worth it for the housing loans, savings dividends, and calamity loans. Small monthly contributions that quietly add up.

protocol.title: Learning without proof is just entertainment.
protocol.lead: The mistake is not picking the wrong course. It is finishing five of them and having nothing to show a client. A resource only counts once it turns into evidence. Run every item on this shelf through the same five moves.

steps.title: Pick one, tied to your niche
steps.desc: Not five. One resource, aimed at the exact outcome your chosen lane needs. Breadth feels productive and builds nothing. Depth in one lane is what gets hired.

steps.title: Set the outcome before you start
steps.desc: Decide what you will have built when you finish, a landing page, a reconciled sample ledger, a month of content, not complete the course. A topic never ends. A deliverable does.

steps.title: Build as you go, not after
steps.desc: Pause the video and do the thing on your own file. Passive watching is the illusion of learning. The part where you are stuck is the part where it is actually happening.

steps.title: Collect proof, not certificates
steps.desc: A certificate is a receipt that says you attended. A portfolio piece is evidence that you can do the work. Clients hire the second one. Turn every course into a thing you can show.

steps.title: Use it on a real task fast
steps.desc: Put the new skill to work within a week: a micro-task, a no-cost project for a cause you like, a rebuild from scratch. A skill you do not use within days is a skill you are about to forget.

closing.title: Access was never the thing standing between you and this career.
closing.body: Everything you need to start is on this shelf, at no cost, right now. What is scarce is not the courses. It is the judgment to pick the right one, the discipline to finish it, and the habit of turning every hour of study into something a client can see. Those are no-cost too. They just are not easy, and that is exactly why the people who build them win.
closing.point: Start with one. Finish it with something built. Then come back for the next.
